artifacts.summary: Confirms the harness's own generic subagent 'Notes:' boilerplate directly contradicts general-research-agent.md's mandatory report-file requirement (observed verbatim in this dispatch's own system prompt); documents postflight's current verdict=failed handling for a missing-report dispatch (status is never falsely advanced, but no defect is recorded and message-borne findings are discarded); and shows the absorbed former-task-195 handoff-writer-predicate defect shares a single root fix with this task's own detection gap.

memory_candidates.content: The Claude Code harness appends a generic, subagent-type-independent 'Notes:' block to Agent-tool subagent system prompts (e.g. 'Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message'). This can directly contradict an agent contract whose sole deliverable is a file (e.g. general-research-agent's mandatory report + .return-meta.json). It is not present in the source-store agent file, the deployed agent file, or settings.json -- it originates from the harness itself, outside agent-system/**. Agent contracts whose only product is a file should include an explicit override statement naming this class of conflict, not just a positive MUST DO, since a plain MUST DO evidently loses a probabilistic priority contest against a later generic contradicting instruction in the same prompt.

In orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, is_contractual_handoff_writer()'s agent-name allowlist is consulted only in the double-miss branch (handoff absent AND .return-meta.json recovery declined). Because skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's Move 2 supplies handoff_path only to dispatch[] rows and Move 3 loops only over dispatch[] rows (aux_dispatch[] never reaches postflight), every agent that reaches this script today was, by construction, expected to be able to write a handoff-equivalent outcome. A hardcoded two-name allowlist here is drift-prone; deriving writer-expectation from dispatch-row shape (or simply 'reached postflight at all') closes detection gaps for every non-allowlisted lifecycle agent at once, since the predicate's false branch currently only WARNs and never records a defect.

context/contracts/recovery.md is exclusively about git fix-forward/rollback discipline (the three-rung Recovery Ladder for RED build states) -- it does not define [PARTIAL] task-status semantics for a dispatch outcome. A task description or dispatch that cites recovery.md for '[PARTIAL] status marking after a missing deliverable' is citing the wrong file; use context/standards/status-markers.md instead.
